title: Software and Code
objective: After this level you can explain what code is and how programs tell a computer what to do.
summary: Software is the instructions that tell hardware what to do. Processors run only binary machine code, so compilers translate languages like Python.

cards.headline: Install an app and your phone learns a new trick. Not one part changed.
cards.body: The phone's parts are the same before and after. What changed was a set of instructions. Those instructions are software, and writing them is called coding.

cards.headline: Hardware and software
cards.body: Hardware is the physical machine: the chips, the screen, the case. Software is the instructions that tell it what to do, bundled into programs. Level 51's programmable computer is a machine that runs software. A new program doesn't change a single transistor. It changes what the transistors are told to do.

cards.headline: The processor only speaks binary
cards.body: A processor runs just one kind of instruction: machine code, written in Level 52's 0s and 1s. People find it very hard to read and write. So programmers use high-level languages such as Python or Java, which are much easier to read and write. Then something has to translate.

cards.headline: Compilers: the translators
cards.body: A compiler translates a whole program into machine code, saved to run whenever it's needed. An interpreter translates and runs it one instruction at a time instead. Grace Hopper designed one of the first compilers after joining the Eckert-Mauchly Computer Corporation in 1949. In 1957 her team's Flow-Matic became the first compiler for business data work written in English words.

cards.headline: Code: compiled
learned: Hardware is the machine; software is its instructions
Processors only run binary machine code
People write in languages like Python and Java
Compilers and interpreters translate; Grace Hopper built an early compiler

questions.prompt: What name covers the programs and instructions that tell a computer what to do?

options.label: Hardware
options.rationale: Hardware is the physical machine that runs them.

options.label: Circuitry
options.rationale: Circuits are part of the hardware.

questions.explanation: Software is the instructions that tell a computer what to do; hardware is the machine itself.

questions.prompt: Why do programmers usually write in a language like Python instead of in machine code?

options.label: Python runs without any processor
options.rationale: Every program still runs on a processor.

options.label: It is far easier for people, and gets translated to machine code
Machine code was banned in 1957
options.rationale: Machine code is still what every processor runs.

questions.explanation: High-level languages are much easier for people to read and write; a compiler or interpreter turns them into machine code.

questions.prompt: Level 52 said computers work in 0s and 1s. What does a compiler turn a Python-style program into?

options.label: Plain English sentences
options.rationale: That runs the other way: toward people, not the processor.

options.label: Magnetized patches on a disk
options.rationale: That describes how a hard drive stores bits.

options.label: A list of pixel colors
options.rationale: Pixels are how pictures are stored.

questions.explanation: Processors only run machine code, which is written in binary; the compiler does that translation.
